notes: Alico Inc. (NASDAQ: ALCO). Florida-based agribusiness historically focused on citrus production (Alico Citrus segment) and land management. In January 2025 management announced a strategic transformation: wind-down of citrus operations after the 2024-25 harvest and pivot to a land-development / asset-light model. Fiscal year ends September 30. Two reportable segments: Alico Citrus (revenue from oranges sold to Tropicana/Florida's Natural under multi-year supply contracts) and Land Management & Other Operations (cattle grazing, hunting leases, mining royalties, real estate). Data from SEC EDGAR (CIK 0000003545) 10-K and 10-Q filings. Net debt = total debt (mortgage + RLOC + term notes with MetLife / Rabo) less cash. EBITDA computed as operating income + D&A unless company-disclosed Adjusted EBITDA; FY24-25 results materially impacted by Hurricane Ian (Sept 2022) USDA RMA crop-insurance and FDOC-block-grant proceeds, plus citrus-greening-driven yield declines. Acreage: peak ~125k acres of land owned (consolidated), with ~48k-50k of citrus groves (now declining to zero) and balance pasture / open / ranchland. Pre-FY19 history: Alico filed 10-Ks back to FY1995 (CIK 0000003545); historical structure was very different — through FY2010 Alico held the historic ~135k-acre Alico Ranch in Hendry/Collier Counties (cattle, sugarcane, vegetables, citrus, mining royalties from Florida Rock / others, sand/rock). November 2010 acquired the ~12k-acre 734 Citrus Holdings (Tropicana grower) for $114M making citrus dominant; 2014 acquired Silver Nip Citrus (~$367M cash + stock) and Orange-Co (~$214M) tripling citrus footprint and shedding most non-citrus operations. FY12-18 backfill from 10-K Selected Financial Data tables; FY95-FY11 from 10-K filings (audited).
